_comment: The English sentence for each documented quarter, keyed by year|season. The chronicle itself — zones held, sources, confidence — is in front-history.json and is never copied here: a position of the front exists only once. A key matching no documented quarter fails the load, and a quarter left empty here falls back to its French sentence.

headlines.2021|Autumn: Nothing moves: the 2014 line, Crimea and the two Donbas enclaves. A hundred thousand men mass on the borders without a shot being fired.
headlines.2022|Winter: The invasion of 24 February on four axes. In the north, the Kyiv column reaches Hostomel, Bucha and Irpin; Chernihiv and Sumy are bypassed and besieged. In the south, Melitopol falls on 1 March and Kherson on the 2nd. Mariupol is encircled as early as 2 March. Occupation peaks at some 120,000 km² in mid-March.
headlines.2022|Spring: The withdrawal from the north is completed between 1 and 6 April: Kyiv, Chernihiv and Sumy are liberated. It is a command decision, not a broken front — the manoeuvre failed, it was not overrun. Izium falls on 1 April, Lyman on 27 May, Mariupol surrenders on 20 May, Sievierodonetsk on 25 June.
headlines.2022|Summer: Lysychansk falls on 3 July, completing the conquest of Luhansk oblast; Russia takes an operational pause. Then the Kharkiv breakthrough, from 6 to 12 September: Balakliia, Izium and Kupiansk are retaken in a week, some 6,000 km² regained. The battle of Bakhmut opens on 1 August.
headlines.2022|Autumn: Lyman is retaken on 1 October. On 11 November, Russia completes the evacuation of right-bank Kherson and the Dnipro becomes the line — the only oblast capital retaken in the whole war. The southern front will not move again for two years.
headlines.2023|Winter: Soledar falls in January, Bakhmut is almost encircled but holds. Everywhere else the line is motionless: the Russian winter offensive exhausts itself at Vuhledar, where two naval infantry brigades are destroyed without gaining a village.
headlines.2023|Spring: Bakhmut falls on 20 May after ten months of siege, at a cost in Russian losses unmatched anywhere in the war. The Ukrainian counter-offensive opens on 4 June and runs within days into the minefields of the Surovikin line.
headlines.2023|Summer: The counter-offensive reaches Robotyne on 22 August and stops there. Some 370 km² retaken in four months, to a depth of about ten kilometres: the second Russian line is never reached. On the flanks of Bakhmut, Klishchiivka and Andriivka are retaken in mid-September.
headlines.2023|Autumn: The counter-offensive dies out without a breakthrough. Russia takes back the initiative at Avdiivka on 10 October. Ukraine establishes a bridgehead at Krynky, on the left bank of the Dnipro — a few square kilometres, held at a heavy price, which do not change control of the bank.
headlines.2024|Winter: Avdiivka falls on 17 February for want of shells: the blockage of American aid in Congress is at its deepest and the garrison withdraws under fire. The first large town lost since Bakhmut.
headlines.2024|Spring: On 10 May, Russia opens a cross-border front north of Kharkiv — Vovchansk and Lyptsi — to stretch the Ukrainian defence. The advance stops a few kilometres from the border and becomes an active defence as early as 23 May. The American aid vote of 24 April begins to take effect.
headlines.2024|Summer: On 6 August, Ukraine crosses the border and takes Sudzha: some 1,000 km² of Kursk oblast in a week, the only Russian ground ever held by the defender. Meanwhile Russia advances on Pokrovsk and retakes the whole of Robotyne at the end of July, erasing the 2023 gain. Ukraine evacuates the Krynky bridgehead.
headlines.2024|Autumn: Vuhledar falls on 1 October after two years of failed sieges. The Kursk salient shrinks: supported by North Korean troops committed from November, Russia has retaken about half of it before the end of the month.
headlines.2025|Winter: Kurakhove on 6 January, Velyka Novosilka on the 26th: the southern Donetsk pocket closes, then the sector stabilises. On 11 March, Ukraine loses Sudzha and most of the Kursk salient — the Russian counter-attack intensifies on 6 March, the day after American aid and intelligence sharing are suspended.
headlines.2025|Spring: On 26 April, Moscow declares Kursk oblast reconquered; residual Ukrainian positions still hold at Tetkino in May, and Putin himself admits on 30 April that Ukrainian soldiers are still there. In mirror image, Russia opens a buffer zone in Sumy oblast: more than 200 km² by June, some twenty kilometres from the city.
headlines.2025|Summer: Chasiv Yar falls on 31 July and opens the Donetsk “fortress belt”. On 11 August, a Russian infiltration pushes fifteen kilometres towards Dobropillia, north of Pokrovsk, and threatens the logistics of the whole sector; Ukraine commits its elite reserves there. The battle of Kupiansk opens in the east.
headlines.2025|Autumn: The Dobropillia salient is entirely erased on 29 November — the only Ukrainian offensive success of the year. Russia claims Kupiansk on 20 November and Pokrovsk on 2 December; Ukraine counter-attacks in both towns and states on 12 December that the attackers in Kupiansk are cut off. In December, Russian troops enter Lyman and probably take Siversk; in the south they push towards Huliaipole.
headlines.2026|Winter: Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad fall: no Ukrainian activity is observed in the town after 28 January, and the ISW concludes on 25 February that it has been taken. No breakthrough follows — the town had ceased to be a logistics hub as early as the summer of 2025. At Kupiansk the claims cancel each other out: the Russian command says it holds the whole town in January, while its own military bloggers see only “a few pockets” there. The Ukrainian counter-attacks of late January in the south block the Orikhiv–Huliaipole junction.
headlines.2026|Spring: The Russian spring offensive comes to nothing: 30.42 km² gained in June 2026 against 481.25 km² in June 2025, that is 1.01 km² a day instead of 16.04. Kostiantynivka is threatened with envelopment, Lyman holds, and the southern front is stabilised by Ukrainian counter-attacks.
headlines.2026|Summer: An incomplete quarter, closed on 13 August 2026. Russia pays in July its highest casualty rate of the year without advancing a single kilometre faster. Lyman is still holding on 18 July, the Huliaipole axis is blocked on 12 August, and on 7 August the ISW judges the Russian objective of taking the whole of Donbas before the end of the year “extremely unrealistic”. Russia controls about 19% of Ukrainian territory, Crimea included.
